messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Spike in 5xxs for tenant thalia (dedicated VPC) on model rwlm-3.2-int in ap-southeast-1. 5xx up to 6.9% over 5m (baseline 0.2%). Auto-pager to #incidents oncall.

Tasha: Taking command. Paging eng-runtime + eng-ml. @ravi @mina please join. @calvin can you send a quick holding note to Thalia SRE?

Ravi: On it. Reading runtime traces now. Seeing repeated "KV shard checksum mismatch" followed by GPU kernel aborts from the int8 load path. This appears isolated to pool thalia-dedicated-01. Recent kernel bump at 02:58 UTC touched the kv schema.

Mina: That matches an ML-side change that tightened KV checksum semantics for quantized weights. Fast mitigation is tenant-level routing to a stable safe variant that uses legacy loader: rwlm-3.1-int-legacy. Quality delta should be minimal for typical prompts.

Tasha: Let's do a canary (10% for 45s) then promote if clean. Also throttle concurrency to protect the pool. Keep the original model paused for the tenant until we verify.

Ravi: Executing runbook commands now:
```
# apply tenant-specific override + concurrency limit
redwoodctl routing create --tenant thalia --override-id ov-thalia-2026a --target rwlm-3.1-int-legacy --strategy canary --percent 10 --duration 45s
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant thalia --concurrency-limit 30
```
Ops-bot: Canary started for tenant thalia -> rwlm-3.1-int-legacy (10%) at 1942001202. Health window 45s.

Ravi: Canary shards show no KV checksum errors; metrics look stable. Promoting to 100% now.

ops-bot: Rollout complete: 100% traffic routed to rwlm-3.1-int-legacy at 1942001249. rwlm-3.2-int paused for tenant thalia (override: ov-thalia-2026a).

Calvin: Holding note sent to Thalia SRE (ticket TH-9916): "We observed increased errors and temporarily routed your tenant to a compatible model variant to restore service. You may notice slight output differences. We're investigating and will share an ETA to return to rwlm-3.2-int." They acknowledged and requested an ETA for the fix.

Tasha: Monitoring: error rate down to 0.3% within 6m, latency unchanged. Good.

Mina: Quick triage items: 
- eng-ml: add a compatibility shim to the int loader that accepts v2/v3 kv checksums and logs mismatches (P0).
- eng-runtime: implement tenant-level auto-fallback for dedicated/VPC pools (threshold suggestion: 1% 5xx over 5m) and make override IDs visible in route metrics (P1).
- support: schedule validation window with Thalia SRE and prepare communication for controlled revert (P1).

Ravi: Capturing artifacts before we rotate anything else:
```
redwoodctl debug pool-dump --pool thalia-dedicated-01 --out /var/tmp/thalia-pool-dump.tgz
redwoodctl debug kv-export --pool thalia-dedicated-01 --pattern "thalia/*" --format text > /var/tmp/thalia-kv-export.log
redwoodctl logs grep --pool thalia-dedicated-01 --filter "checksum" > /var/tmp/thalia-kv-checks.log
```
support-bot: Artifacts attached to incident record: [/var/tmp/thalia-pool-dump.tgz, /var/tmp/thalia-kv-export.log, /var/tmp/thalia-kv-checks.log].

Jordan: I'll take overnight monitoring. Handoff: override ov-thalia-2026a active, watch for any quality regressions reported by Thalia, and ensure the override ID is pinned in dashboards. Contact: jordan@redwood. If 5xx >1% while override active, re-escalate to eng-ml.

Tasha: Thanks Jordan. Leaving a concise summary for PIR: tenant routed to legacy-safe variant, artifacts collected, eng-ml to ship shim, eng-runtime to add auto-fallback config. Marking mitigated for now.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated for tenant thalia at 1942001877. Severity: customer-impacting -> mitigated. Please open PIR and attach artifacts and override ID ov-thalia-2026a.

Calvin: Creating customer-facing post-incident note template and PIR ticket. We'll propose a low-traffic revert window once eng-ml validates the shim.

Mina: Plan for next 24h: develop shim, run unit + integration tests against pool snapshot, then coordinate a non-customer canary redeploy. If tests pass, schedule coordinated revert with Thalia during agreed maintenance window.

Tasha: Closing this thread for now. Good job team. :thumbsup:
